formation.title: The Kingdom of Nepal
formation.text:
From the snow-crowned peaks of the Himalaya to the steaming jungles of the Terai, a new kingdom takes shape. For centuries, the hills of Nepal harbored dozens of warring principalities: the Baisi and Chaubisi kingdoms, the three Malla city-states of the Kathmandu Valley, and countless petty lordships scattered across the ridges. Now they answer to a single crown.

The question before us is not whether Nepal shall endure, the mountains themselves guarantee that, but what kind of kingdom it shall become. The warriors of Gorkha who united these hills by force of arms see a martial destiny: Nepal as an unconquerable mountain fortress, its soldiers the terror of every invader who dares the passes. But the Newari craftsmen and merchants of the Valley see another path: Nepal as a bridge between civilizations, its temples drawing pilgrims, its workshops producing art that rivals any in Asia, its traders carrying salt and wool and silk across the roof of the world.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Gorkhali: the mountains are our sword and shield.

modifiers.name: Gorkhali Conquest
modifiers.text: The warriors of Gorkha have proven that mountains breed the fiercest soldiers. With khukuri in hand and the Himalayan winds at their back, the Gorkhali armies sweep through the valleys, conquering all who stand before them.

options.text: The Valley of Temples shall be the jewel of the Himalaya.

modifiers.name: Valley of Temples
modifiers.text: The Kathmandu Valley stands as a living museum of divine architecture. Newari craftsmen have raised pagodas toward heaven, and the trade routes that thread through these sacred precincts carry wealth from Tibet to India.

advances.name: Khas Warriors
advances.text: The Khas Malla empire of western Nepal produced fierce warriors who raided as far as Tibet and the Kathmandu Valley between the 12th and 14th centuries.

advances.name: Newari Architecture
advances.text: The Newar people of the Kathmandu Valley developed a distinctive architectural tradition of multi-tiered pagoda temples, intricately carved wooden struts, and brick-and-timber construction.

advances.name: Trans-Himalayan Trade
advances.text: For millennia, trade routes have threaded through the Himalayan passes, carrying salt and wool from Tibet southward and grain and manufactured goods northward.

advances.name: Himalayan Herbs
advances.text: The foothills of the Himalaya produce an extraordinary variety of medicinal herbs and plants, traded throughout South Asia for centuries. With them goes musk, cut from the deer of the high forests and prized by every physician and perfumer of the plains.

advances.name: Mountain Dwellers
advances.text: Life in the Himalayan hills breeds hardiness. Armies that invade these heights face exhaustion, altitude sickness, and impassable terrain before ever meeting a Nepali soldier.

advances.name: Malla Governance
advances.text: The Malla kings developed sophisticated administrative systems for governing the three city-states of the Kathmandu Valley, with codified laws and court traditions.

advances.name: Patan Metalwork
advances.text: The city of Patan, the ancient capital of Lalitpur, is renowned for its metalworking tradition. Newar artisans produce bronze sculptures and religious objects of extraordinary quality.

advances.name: Guthi System
advances.text: The guthi are communal trust endowments that fund temples, festivals, and social welfare. This institution strengthens community bonds and ensures continuity of religious and cultural life.

advances.name: Pashmina Trade
advances.text: The fine wool of Himalayan mountain goats is woven into pashmina, prized across South Asia and beyond for its warmth and delicacy. The looms stand in the herding villages of the wool country.

advances.name: Durbar Squares
advances.text: The royal palace squares of Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, and Patan are centers of political power and artistic achievement, filled with temples, courtyards, and carved monuments.

advances.name: Arniko's Legacy
advances.text: The 13th-century Newar architect Arniko carried Nepal's pagoda architectural tradition to the Yuan court, where it transformed building practices across East Asia.

event.title: Arniko and the Pagoda Legacy
event.text:
In 1260, the young Newar architect Arniko led a delegation of eighty artisans from the Kathmandu Valley to the court of Kublai Khan in China. The Emperor, having heard of the extraordinary skill of Newari craftsmen in metalwork and temple construction, had requested their services to build a golden stupa in Tibet.

Arniko's genius transcended the original commission. He designed pagodas, cast bronze statues of astonishing beauty, and introduced architectural techniques that would transform building practices across the Yuan Empire. The multi-tiered pagoda style that originated in Nepal's temple squares now rises above Buddhist monasteries from Lhasa to Beijing. Arniko himself became Controller of Imperial Manufactories: a remarkable honor for a foreign artisan.

The legacy endures in every pagoda that graces the skylines of East Asia, a testament to the artistic traditions nurtured in the workshops of Patan and the temple squares of Bhaktapur.

options.text: Our craftsmen carry Nepal's glory to the far corners of the world.

advances.name: Newar Guilds
advances.text: Newar society is organized around occupational guilds and caste groups, with metalworkers, carpenters, painters, and traders each specializing in crafts crucial to valley life.

advances.name: Mountain Fortifications
advances.text: Nepal's mountain passes and ridgelines are natural defensive positions. Fortifying them transforms already difficult terrain into impregnable strongholds.

advances.name: Gorkhali Tradition
advances.text: The soldiers of the Gorkha kingdom combine mountain endurance with fierce discipline. They fight with the khukuri at close quarters and know every ridge and valley of their homeland.

advances.name: Salt Trade
advances.text: The ancient trade in Tibetan salt passes through Nepal's mountain corridors, with Himalayan communities acting as intermediaries between Tibet's pastoral economy and India's agricultural plains. The same pack trains can carry an army's grain over the passes.

advances.name: Malla Renaissance
advances.text:
The later Malla period saw an explosion of artistic achievement in the Kathmandu Valley, with paubha scroll painting, bronze sculpture, and wood carving reaching extraordinary heights under royal patronage.

Available in: Newari Workshop

advances.name: Baisi-Chaubisi Kingdoms
advances.text: Before unification, Nepal was fragmented into the Baisi (twenty-two) and Chaubisi (twenty-four) kingdoms: a patchwork of hill principalities constantly competing through alliance, intrigue, and warfare.

advances.name: Religious Syncretism
advances.text: In the Kathmandu Valley, Hinduism and Buddhism have coexisted and intertwined for centuries. The same deities are worshipped under different names, and temples serve both traditions.

advances.name: Khukuri Warriors
advances.text: The forward-curved khukuri is both tool and weapon, carried by every Gorkhali soldier. In close combat, its heavy chopping blade is devastating, and its fearsome reputation precedes its wielder.

advances.name: Mountain Warfare
advances.text: Centuries of warfare in the hills have produced a distinctive Nepali military doctrine: hold the high ground, control the passes, harry the enemy's supply lines, and fight only when the terrain favors you.

advances.name: Gorkha Consolidation
advances.text: The Shah dynasty of Gorkha transforms a petty hill kingdom into a centralized state, building the military and administrative infrastructure needed for unification.

advances.name: Pajani System
advances.text: The annual pajani review system ensures no official grows complacent. Every year, appointments are reconsidered and land grants reconfirmed, or revoked.

advances.name: Birta Grants
advances.text: Tax-free birta land grants reward military service and administrative loyalty, incentivizing the expansion of the Gorkha army without overtaxing the populace.

advances.name: Valley Commerce
advances.text: The three former Malla city-states of the Kathmandu Valley (Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur) remain thriving commercial centers under the unified kingdom.

advances.name: Gorkha Rifles
advances.text: The introduction of modern firearms transforms the Gorkhali infantry into a formidable force combining European weapons technology with unmatched mountain fighting skill.

advances.name: Shah Unification
advances.text: Prithvi Narayan Shah conquers the Kathmandu Valley in 1768, uniting the scattered hill kingdoms into the Kingdom of Nepal and establishing the Shah dynasty as rulers of a unified state.

event.title: The Unification of Nepal
event.text:
On the 25th of September, 1768, as the people of Kathmandu celebrated the festival of Indra Jatra, the armies of Gorkha entered the city. The Malla king Jaya Prakash Malla fled into the night, and Prithvi Narayan Shah ascended the throne of the Kathmandu Valley. Within a year, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur had also fallen.

The young king who had inherited a tiny hill principality in 1743 had spent twenty-five years in relentless preparation. He sealed alliances, trained his soldiers in mountain warfare, cut off the Valley's trade routes to starve it into submission, and finally struck at the moment of religious celebration when the defenders were distracted. His Dibya Upadesh, the 'Divine Counsel', laid out a political philosophy for governing the diverse peoples of his new kingdom: Nepal as a garden of many flowers, united under the Shah crown.

The fifty-four kingdoms of the hills are now one. The pajani system reviews every official annually. Birta land grants reward the loyal. Twelve districts, four in each region, carry the king's authority to every corner of the realm.

options.text: Nepal is now one kingdom, from Mechi to Mahakali.

modifiers.name: Unification of Nepal
modifiers.text: The scattered kingdoms of the hills have been forged into one nation by the iron will of the Shah dynasty. The twelve districts answer to a single throne, and the administration of Nepal flows from a unified center.

advances.name: The Six Houses
advances.text: Six houses of Gorkha, the Pande, Pantha, Aryal, Khanal, Rana and Bohora, have stood beside the Shah kings since the kingdom was founded. As the realm grows, its high offices are filled from these Tharghar, and the court that is kept in their hands is kept in order.

advances.name: Mission to Peking
advances.text: By the peace made at Betrawati in 1792 an embassy is sent over the passes to Peking every five years with gifts for the emperor. The favour of a distant court costs little, and it is weighed by every power in the plains that thinks of marching into the hills.

advances.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
advances.text: The 1814-1816 war with the British East India Company costs Nepal a third of its territory but earns the Gurkha a reputation as the fiercest infantry in Asia.

event.title: The Anglo-Nepalese War
event.text:
The expanding borders of Nepal have collided with the interests of the British East India Company. In 1814, after years of frontier skirmishes and disputed territories in the Terai, war has broken out. The Company fields armies numbering thirty thousand men with modern artillery; Nepal's defenders number barely eight thousand.

But the Gurkhas fight on their own ground. General Amar Singh Thapa holds the western passes with stubborn determination. The British columns find their cannons useless in the mountains, their supply lines harassed by Gurkha raiders, their soldiers dropping from disease and exhaustion. It takes the most experienced British commander, David Ochterlony, two years and an innovative mountain campaign to finally force a decisive battle at Makwanpur.

The Treaty of Sugauli costs Nepal a third of its territory, but it gains something perhaps more valuable. The British, who have fought across India and the world, declare the Gurkha the most formidable infantry they have ever faced. They will never attempt to conquer Nepal again.

options.text: Our mountains are our greatest fortress. Let us fortify every pass.

modifiers.name: Himalayan Bastion
modifiers.text: The mountains themselves are our fortress. Every pass is a deathtrap, every ridge a rampart. Foreign armies that march into these hills find that the terrain fights for Nepal before a single Gorkhali blade is drawn.

options.text: The world has seen what a Gurkha can do. Let that reputation be our shield.

modifiers.name: Gurkha Renown
modifiers.text: The bravery of the Gurkha soldier has become legend. Their discipline under fire, their fearless charges with drawn khukuri, and their tireless endurance in the most punishing terrain have earned respect across the world.

advances.name: Rana Modernization
advances.text: The Rana prime ministers who dominate Nepal's government from 1846 onward introduce military reforms modeled on European armies while maintaining Nepal's fierce independence. The arsenals begun under Bhimsen Thapa supply the muskets.

advances.name: Himalayan Sovereignty
advances.text: Nepal stands as one of the few Asian states never colonized by a European power. Its mountain geography, martial reputation, and diplomatic skill preserve its independence.

advances.name: Mountain Kingdom Identity
advances.text: The diverse peoples of Nepal (Newar, Magar, Gurung, Limbu, Rai, Chhetri, and others) forge a shared identity as citizens of the mountain kingdom.

destiny.name: Destiny of Nepal
destiny.text: The Kingdom of Nepal has been proclaimed. Now begins the true test: can this mountain kingdom forge a lasting destiny among the great powers of Asia? Achieve stability to set the foundations.

event.title: The Mountain Kingdom Rises
event.text:
Nepal stands united: a single crown above the land of snow and temple. The scattered principalities that once warred among themselves have been forged into a kingdom. From the Terai jungles to the high Himalayan passes, the flag of Nepal flies.

But a kingdom newly born must prove its worth. The court debates the path forward: shall Nepal be a sword or a jewel? A mountain fortress whose warriors terrify empires, or a garden of temples whose artisans and merchants earn the admiration of the world?

The foundations are laid. What rises upon them depends on the choices yet to come.

options.text: Nepal shall endure: this we swear upon the mountains.

destiny.name: Conquest of the Hills
destiny.text: The Gorkhali sword must first unite the foothills. Seize the sacred ground of Lumbini and push into the Mithila plains at Darbhanga. Build an army worthy of mountain warriors.

conditions.text: Own Lumbini, or a subject owns it
Own Darbhanga, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Hills Submit
event.text:
The birth-soil of the Buddha at Lumbini now falls under Nepali sovereignty, and our armies have pushed across the Terai into the Mithila plains. The sacred sites and fertile lowlands that once fed rival kingdoms now sustain the Gorkhali war machine.

Local zamindars and petty rajas bend the knee or flee. The mountain warriors who once fought only among ridges and valleys have proven they can descend into the flatlands and conquer there too. Every hill fort and river crossing reinforces the lesson: the Gorkhali do not stop.

options.text: The foothills are ours. Now: the plains.

destiny.name: Descent to the Plains
destiny.text: With the hills secure, the Gorkhali gaze turns south to the rich Gangetic plain. Raise standing companies under paid officers, and Patna and Lucknow, seats of ancient empires, must fall to Nepali arms.

conditions.text: Own Patna, or a subject owns it
Own Lucknow, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Conquest of the Plains
event.text:
Patna, the ancient capital of Magadha, has fallen to Gorkhali arms. Lucknow, seat of the Nawabs of Awadh, follows. The mountain warriors who once seemed content with their highland kingdom have burst forth into the Gangetic heartland like a Himalayan river breaking its banks.

The conquests present a choice. We can push rapidly, sweeping through the Terai and the plains with aggressive campaigns that seize territory before our enemies can organize: speed and violence carrying the day. Or we can advance methodically, securing supply lines through the mountain passes and binding conquered peoples to Nepali rule through loyal vassals and garrison settlements.

options.text: Strike fast: speed is our weapon now.

modifiers.name: Sweep of the Terai
modifiers.text: The Gorkhali armies have swept through the Terai lowlands with devastating speed, but the rapid expansion strains the kingdom's treasury.

options.text: Secure each valley before advancing to the next.

modifiers.name: Mountain Descent
modifiers.text: Nepal's advance into the plains proceeds methodically, with supply lines secured through the mountain passes and conquered territories bound through loyal vassals.

destiny.name: The Gorkhali Empire
destiny.text: The ultimate vision: a Himalayan empire stretching from the rooftop of the world to the holy waters of the Ganges. Take Lhasa, the sacred city of Tibet, and Varanasi, holiest city of Hinduism.

conditions.text: Own Lhasa, or a subject owns it
Own Varanasi, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Gorkhali Empire
event.text:
From the golden rooftops of Lhasa to the burning ghats of Varanasi, the flag of Nepal flies over lands that have humbled every conqueror in history. The Potala Palace and the Vishwanath Temple, the holiest sites of Buddhism and Hinduism alike, acknowledge Nepali sovereignty.

This is no mere hill kingdom. This is an empire that bestrides the Himalaya, controlling the trade routes between India and Central Asia, commanding the sacred geography of two great faiths, and fielding armies hardened by the most demanding terrain on earth.

The question now is how to rule. Shall Nepal extract the tribute of the conqueror, or absorb these diverse peoples into a mountain civilization that transcends any single culture?

options.text: The conquered shall know the price of Gorkhali might.

modifiers.name: Nepal Ascendant
modifiers.text: The Gorkhali empire is a reality. Nepal dictates terms from a position of absolute strength, its armies enriched by the spoils of conquest.

options.text: Let every people find their place within the mountain empire.

modifiers.name: The Mountain Empire
modifiers.text: The diverse peoples of the Gorkhali empire are being drawn into a shared mountain civilization, though Nepal's fearsome reputation makes diplomacy difficult.

destiny.name: Trans-Himalayan Trade
destiny.text: Control the trade routes that thread through the mountain passes. Seize Shigatse in Tibet to dominate the northern approach, and ensure silk flows through Nepali markets.

conditions.text: Own Shigatse, or a subject owns it
A market the country is in

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

event.title: The Trade Routes Open
event.text:
Nepali merchants now control Shigatse, the great trading town of Tsang province in Tibet. Silk caravans from China and India pass through markets where Newari traders weigh goods and set prices. The ancient dream of Nepal as a bridge between civilizations begins to take form.

Salt flows south, grain flows north, and silk from both directions meets in Kathmandu's market squares. The sarais along the mountain passes bustle with traders speaking a dozen languages. Nepal's geographic position, once seen as a curse trapped between empires, reveals itself as the kingdom's greatest asset.

options.text: The mountains do not divide. They connect.

destiny.name: The Artisan Flowering
destiny.text: The workshops of the Valley must become legendary. Spread to Paro in Bhutan, build up Kathmandu, and found a library there to keep the manuscripts of a renaissance of craft and learning.

conditions.text: We own Kathmandu and its development is at least 38
Own Paro, or a subject owns it
We own Kathmandu and a Library stands there

event.title: The Artisan Flowering
event.text:
The workshops of Patan and Bhaktapur have entered a golden age. Bronze sculptures of extraordinary delicacy, paubha paintings alive with mineral pigments, and wood carvings of impossible intricacy flow from Newari workshops to courts and temples across Asia. The new library of Kathmandu fills with copies of religious texts and artistic manuals.

Nepal's cultural reach now extends to Bhutan, where Nepali-trained artisans build temples in the Newari style. The kingdom must decide how to sustain this flowering: through the discipline of guild regulation, ensuring quality through tradition, or through open markets that attract foreign artisans and ideas.

options.text: The guilds shall guard the standard of Newari craft.

modifiers.name: Guild of the Valley
modifiers.text: The Newar guilds enforce exacting standards that make Valley craftsmanship legendary. Cheap credit flows to workshops, but the focus on craft has weakened the kingdom's cavalry arm.

options.text: Open the passes. Let trade carry our art to the world.

modifiers.name: Himalayan Silk Road
modifiers.text: Nepal sits at the crossroads of civilizations, its markets open to traders of every faith and nation. The mountain passes carry wealth in both directions.

destiny.name: Jewel of the Himalaya
destiny.text: The Kathmandu Valley shall become the cultural jewel of Asia. Extend Nepal's civilizing influence to Thimpu, give the Newar merchant houses a quarter of their own in Kathmandu, and ensure Newari jewelry graces the markets of the world.

conditions.text: Own Thimpu, or a subject owns it
We own Kathmandu and Merchants Quarters or a building that replaced them stand there
A market the country is in

children.text: Jewelry is produced in the market
Jewelry is traded in the market

event.title: Jewel of the Himalaya
event.text:
The Kathmandu Valley has become what Arniko's journey to the Yuan court only hinted at: the cultural and spiritual center of the Himalayan world. Newari jewelry, cast in workshops that have refined their techniques over centuries, is traded as far as Persia and Siam. Temples rise in the pagoda style from Bhutan to Bengal, all tracing their lineage to the master builders of Patan.

Scholars come to study at institutions where Hindu philosophy and Buddhist meditation are taught side by side. The Valley's syncretism, once a local curiosity, has become a model for religious harmony that draws admiration from far beyond the mountains.

Nepal must choose how to project this cultural power: through diplomatic engagement that opens doors across the world, or through deepening the Valley's role as a sacred center of pilgrimage and learning.

options.text: Let Nepal's voice be heard in every court of Asia.

modifiers.name: Himalayan Jewel
modifiers.text: Nepal's cultural diplomacy opens doors across Asia. Ambassadors and scholars carry the Valley's renown to every court, and new ideas flow back along the same channels.

options.text: The Valley itself shall be the destination. Let the world come to us.

modifiers.name: The Sacred Valley
modifiers.text: The Kathmandu Valley has become a center of religious harmony and learning, where Hindu and Buddhist traditions enrich each other under a streamlined administration. Pilgrims and scholars of both come to it, and many stay.

units.name: Khas Warrior
units.text: Fierce mountain infantry of the ancient Khas Malla empire, hardened by constant warfare across the western Himalayan ridges.

units.name: Gorkhali Sipahi
units.text: Disciplined soldiers of the Gorkha kingdom, trained in mountain warfare and armed with the distinctive khukuri alongside conventional weapons.

units.name: Khukuri Skirmisher
units.text: Close-combat raiders who exploit the confusion of mountain warfare, closing rapidly with their heavy khukuri blades to devastating effect. They wear no armour.

units.name: Yak Caravan
units.text: The pack trains of the salt trade, pressed into the army's service: yaks on the high passes, sheep and goats with saddlebags below. They carry more than a cart column and are slowed less by mountain and hill, and they are slow everywhere.

units.name: Gorkha Rifleman
units.text: The modernized mountain infantry of Nepal, combining European firearms with the endurance, discipline, and terrain mastery that make Gurkha soldiers legendary.

buildings.name: Pagoda Temple
buildings.text: A multi-tiered temple in the distinctive Newari architectural style, with intricately carved wooden struts, brick walls, and gilded rooftops rising toward the heavens.

buildings.name: Himalayan Fortress
buildings.text: A mountain stronghold built to control a strategic pass or ridge, exploiting the natural defensive advantages of Nepal's rugged terrain.

buildings.name: Himalayan Sarai
buildings.text: A rest house and trading post along the trans-Himalayan trade routes, providing shelter and storage for the caravans that carry salt, wool, and grain between Tibet and India.

buildings.name: Herb Gatherers' Lodge
buildings.text: Drying sheds at the edge of the hill forest. The hunters and collectors of the valley bring in musk pods, hides, roots and herbs each season, and the lodge sorts, dries and packs them for the physicians and perfumers of the plains, so more of what the forest yields reaches the market. It can stand only where the land is rich in game.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wild Game

buildings.name: Hill Loom House
buildings.text: A house of looms in a herding village, where the under-wool of mountain goats is combed out, spun and woven into shawl cloth. It can stand only in wool country.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wool

buildings.name: Newari Workshop
buildings.text: A metalworking and woodcarving workshop staffed by Newar artisans, producing bronze sculptures, religious objects, and architectural elements of extraordinary craftsmanship.

buildings.name: Guthi Endowment
buildings.text: A communal trust institution that manages land endowments to fund temples, festivals, and social welfare. The guthi system is the bedrock of Newar community life.

buildings.name: Durbar Palace
buildings.text: A royal palace complex in the Malla tradition, with courtyards, audience halls, and surrounding temples that serve as the political and cultural heart of a Nepali city.

buildings.name: Gorkhali Barracks
buildings.text: A military training facility where mountain infantry learn the combat techniques that make Gorkhali soldiers feared throughout the subcontinent.

buildings.name: Gorkhali Arsenal
buildings.text: A gun foundry and magazine of the state. Smiths work iron from the hill mines into musket barrels and locks on foreign patterns, and the finished arms are stored under guard.

buildings.name: Gorkhali Citadel
buildings.text: A massive mountain citadel built to project Gorkhali power across conquered territory, with barracks, armories, and command posts for the empire's ever-expanding armies.

buildings.name: Valley Academy
buildings.text: A center of learning where Hindu philosophy, Buddhist meditation, and Newari artistic traditions are studied and preserved, attracting scholars from across the Himalayan world.

list.name: Bhardari Sabha
list.text: The bhardari was the council of bhardars: the great noble houses (Pande, Thapa, Basnyat, Chautariya) holding kaji and sardar offices. After Prithvi Narayan Shah's death in 1775, the council effectively ran Nepal during the long minorities of the Shah kings, balancing the throne against the kajis. The Bhardari Sabha is the corporate body of the noble houses; well-tended it stabilises succession, neglected it dissolves into faction war.

list.name: Mukhtiyari
list.text: The mukhtiyar was the all-powerful chief minister of Nepal, an office institutionalised by Bhimsen Thapa from 1806 to 1837 under King Girvan Yuddha and the boy-king Rajendra. Holding the seal, the army, and the treasury, the mukhtiyar superseded the bhardari council and concentrated authority into a single hand: a deliberate executive counter to the noble factions. Maintained, the office moves the kingdom in step; let go, it collapses into a bottleneck and the kajis turn against the upstart.

list.name: Pajani
list.text: The pajani was the annual personnel review at which every civil and military officeholder presented themselves at court for reappointment; tenure expired by default each year. A Shah-era device for keeping the kajis, sardars, and revenue collectors directly accountable to the throne: the institutional opposite of hereditary office. Maintained, the pajani keeps officials sharp; neglected, every position has its price and patronage churn ruins continuity in the provinces.

list.name: Newar Guthi
list.text: The guthi system is the Newari institution of perpetual trusts, held collectively by clans or castes, that fund temple maintenance, festival processions, irrigation channels, and rest-houses. Guthis own land outright and administer it across generations independent of royal patronage. The Malla kings ruled with the guthi system; the Shahs inherited it and were never able to dissolve it. A standing civic-religious infrastructure parallel to the state: when in good order, festivals run and irrigation flows; when neglected, the trustees turn the endowments into private fiefs.

list.name: Jagir Land Tenure
list.text: Jagir was the assignment of revenue from a tract of land to a soldier or officer in lieu of cash pay; held for the term of service and, in principle, revocable at pajani. Alongside birta (tax-free grants to brahmins, often hereditary), jagir provided the financial backbone of the Gorkhali army, letting the kingdom field large forces without a treasury that could pay them. Maintained, the army musters cheaply; neglected, jagirdars squeeze the peasantry and revocable assignments harden into hereditary holdings.
